verdicts.flaw_description: A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "The lubricant supply switched to a higher-grade synthetic mid-cycle, and every machine here drew from that supply." A better lubricant plausibly explains the 260-410 extra hours on all four machines, so the gain cannot be attributed to the redesigned bearing.

The measured population is narrower than the claim: "Rates cover the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol, and a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol." The 9/6/11/7 percent falls are computed on a self-selected 75% subgroup (those never off protocol), not on the ward's infection rate that the claim is about, and the excluded quarter are plausibly the longer/more complicated stays with higher infection risk.

A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "The free trial ran thirty days, four times its length in the earlier period, and every cohort here signed up on that trial." A trial that previously ended after ~7.5 days now runs past day fourteen, which by itself would lift week-two retention for all four cohorts independently of the onboarding email.

Two of the four cases have measurement dates that precede enrolment: cohort One "started 4 April; by 29 March" and cohort Three "started 5 October; by 30 September." Those bpm drops (5 and 6 bpm) were observed before the app was started, so they cannot be effects of it.
